author: Codex attendance_review research author; not an independent language approver
method: Original Oxford and Collins publisher pages opened through the web connector. Oxford sense attributes separately retrieved over HTTP and retained in oxford-html-metadata.json. All descriptions here are authored summaries; no publisher examples, full definitions, media or exercises are imported.
global_limits: Author proposals only. Definitions, examples and editorial difficulty require a separate independent acceptance decision.

The research preserves every original review, morphology, media, region, accepted form, identity, historical reference, editorial note, membership and expression. Proposed notes are separate review material.
Oxford rendered topic labels and HTML attributes are separate observations. Unrelated Word of the Day labels are not assigned to the target. Missing levels mean not observed, not an inferred level.
Collins B1+ is retained literally. It is not silently converted to B1 or B2. Higher or missing source labels are not clamped to the current A2/B1/B2 schema.
No human, subject-matter, whole-expression, morphology, picture, audio, domain, module or release approval is claimed.

entries.selected_sense: Removing an error by changing the thing that contains it, represented by correcting a misspelled company name.
entries.difficulty_rationale: Retain editorial A2 for this narrow error-removal sense: Oxford's selected verb sense has A1 metadata. Collins labels the broader problem/fault-remedy verb B2; this disagreement remains explicit. Collins adjective A2 is not evidence for this verb.
entries.excluded_scope: The adjective meaning accurate, teacher marking, correcting a person, punishment, medical treatment and statistical adjustment remain outside this proposal.
entries.context_boundary: Only the ordinary error-removal verb is proposed. Correct adjective uses, corrected modifiers and specialized record-correction procedures receive no acceptance. Foundation02.04 also contains held verify and remains wholly pending.
entries.proposed_note: Proposed ordinary error-removal verb with the original spelling example and editorial A2. Oxford selected A1 and Collins selected B2 remain distinct evidence. The adjective and all expression, domain, morphology and media decisions remain separate.

sources.summary: The first verb sense concerns making an inaccurate item right; written errors fit. Teacher marking and telling a speaker they are mistaken appear as separate senses.
sources.regional_register: No region or formal-register restriction is shown on the selected verb sense. British and American pronunciation/forms are available.
sources.other_sense_boundary: Sense 2 teacher marking has B1 metadata. The adjective is a separate entry; do not borrow its labels.

sources.summary: The selected verb repairs a mistake or fault. The page separately lists addressing another speaker and a teacher marking writing.
sources.regional_register: The selected verb has no regional label. Formal labels on nearby adjective senses must not be transferred to this verb.
sources.other_sense_boundary: Adjective senses 1 and 2 show A2; those are excluded from the verb-level rationale.

entries.selected_sense: Making a small change to improve suitability or operation, represented by moving a meeting time by ten minutes.
entries.difficulty_rationale: Both Oxford selected sense 1 and Collins selected transitive sense 3 support B2. The draft A2 has no support in these selected observations; propose B2 without changing the definition or example.
entries.excluded_scope: Getting used to circumstances, the Indian English phrase kindly adjust, arranging clothes, eyesight adaptation and insurance-claim adjustment are separate.
entries.context_boundary: Foundation02.07 contains this time adjustment alongside held postpone and cancellation; the expression remains exact and pending.
entries.proposed_note: Proposed ordinary small-change sense with the original meeting-time example and editorial B2. Oxford and Collins selected senses support B2. Adaptation, insurance and regional idioms remain separate; no whole-expression or nonlanguage approval follows.

sources.summary: The first sense makes a modest change for suitability or better operation. This supports the limited change to meeting time in the existing example.
sources.regional_register: The selected sense is not region restricted. The distinct kindly adjust idiom is marked Indian English.
sources.other_sense_boundary: Adaptation is sense 2; tidying clothing is sense 3. Neither expands the selected scope.

sources.summary: The selected sense changes something to improve its effectiveness or suitability. Clothing or machine settings and personal adaptation are listed separately.
sources.regional_register: No regional restriction is shown for the selected ordinary transitive sense.
sources.other_sense_boundary: Insurance assessment appears in a separate British dictionary subsection and is not proposed.

entries.selected_sense: Changing the assigned time or date of an activity that was already planned, represented by a training session.
entries.difficulty_rationale: Collins selected event sense 1 explicitly shows B2. Oxford gives the same event sense but its selected HTML element has neither cefr nor fkcefr and the rendered section has no selected level. Propose B2 from Collins, not from an invented Oxford label.
entries.excluded_scope: Debt repayment restructuring is a separate financial sense. Unlike postpone, event rescheduling does not require every change to be later.
entries.context_boundary: No current expression text or focus ID matches the reschedule inflections. That absence creates no expression approval or binding.
entries.proposed_note: Proposed ordinary event time/date change with the original training-session example and editorial B2 from Collins. Oxford's selected level is unobserved. Financial rescheduling remains excluded; nonlanguage gates remain pending.

sources.summary: A previously planned event gets a different time, often later. The entry commonly uses the passive and distinguishes debt rescheduling as sense 2.
sources.regional_register: British and US pronunciations differ; no regional meaning restriction is shown for event scheduling.
sources.other_sense_boundary: The displayed C2 footer labels the Word of the Day spoiler, not reschedule. No selected level is observed.

sources.summary: The selected sense changes when an event is due. Transitive object and for/to time complements support the retained training example.
sources.regional_register: The page distinguishes US pronunciation; the selected meaning has no regional restriction.
sources.other_sense_boundary: Debt repayment extensions are separately listed in sense 2 and excluded.

entries.selected_sense: Moving a planned activity to a later time, represented by a review deferred until next week.
entries.difficulty_rationale: Oxford selected fkcefr=c1 and the Working life C1 topic are explicit. Collins gives literal B1+. Neither supports retaining draft A2; B1+ is not a schema value, and C1 must not be silently clamped to B2.
entries.hold_reason: Hold the entire entry unchanged pending an independently justified course placement or schema/scope decision. The meaning/example are plausible but level reconciliation has not been accepted.
entries.excluded_scope: Lower-priority ranking and specialist loan-repayment arrangements are outside the ordinary meeting/review example. Postponing requires later timing, unlike general rescheduling.
entries.context_boundary: Foundation02.07 remains pending and contains this held focus ID. Language research does not approve its historically authored post/pone morphology.
entries.proposed_note: Held unchanged. Selected Oxford C1 and Collins B1+ remain literal and unresolved against the current course schema. No note, reference, review gate or other field is proposed for integration.

sources.summary: The selected meaning moves an intended event later. Its patterns include an event object, until/to timing and an -ing activity complement.
sources.regional_register: No regional restriction is displayed for the ordinary delay sense.
sources.other_sense_boundary: The literal HTML attribute is fkcefr, not cefr. Etymological post/pone information does not grant morphology approval.

sources.regional_register: No regional restriction is shown for this selected sense.
sources.other_sense_boundary: B1+ is recorded exactly; no automatic conversion to B1 or B2. A priority-ranking sense occurs in another dictionary section.

entries.selected_sense: Stopping an ordinary planned activity or arrangement from going ahead, represented by cancelling a duplicate booking.
entries.difficulty_rationale: Oxford planned-event sense 1 and stopping-an-arrangement sense 2 both carry B2. Collins combines ordinary planned events and orders/services in its B1+ sense 1. Propose editorial B2 with that literal disagreement retained; B1+ is not rounded.
entries.excluded_scope: Legal validity, debt relief, insurance-policy consequences, stamp/ticket invalidation, social exclusion and mathematical cancel-out meanings are excluded. The booking example claims no authority or cancellation policy.
entries.context_boundary: The existing duplicate booking belongs to ordinary arrangements. Oxford separates event cancellation from ending agreements; the proposal does not merge all their legal consequences. Foundation02.07 remains pending and still includes held postpone.
entries.proposed_note: Proposed ordinary planned-arrangement cancellation with the original duplicate-booking example and editorial B2. Oxford senses 1 and 2 are separately recorded at B2; Collins sense 1 remains B1+. No legal cancellation consequence, inflected-form admission, expression or other gate is approved.

sources.selected_section: Planned-event sense 1, lines 116-126; contrast ordinary agreement/order cancellation in sense 2, lines 129-135
sources.rendered_label_scope: Discussion and agreement topic belongs to sense 2 only; sense 1 level comes from its separate HTML metadata
sources.summary: Sense 1 prevents an arranged event from occurring; sense 2 stops a continuing arrangement or order. Both provide B2 metadata but their scopes are not treated as identical.
sources.regional_register: Base cancel is unrestricted. The forms table distinguishes British cancelled/cancelling from US canceled/canceling; accepted forms and morphology remain unchanged.
sources.other_sense_boundary: Stamp/ticket marking and social exclusion are separate senses; C2 for social exclusion is not this booking decision.

sources.selected_section: COBUILD sense 1 ordinary arrangements/orders, rendered lines 222-233
sources.summary: The first sense stops arranged events or tells a supplier that an order is no longer wanted. This supports the ordinary booking arrangement without asserting legal effects.
sources.regional_register: The forms note explicitly uses canceled/canceling in American English and cancelled/cancelling otherwise. No new scored forms are proposed.
sources.other_sense_boundary: Official invalidation of documents/policies/debt, social exclusion and stamp/cheque marking are separately numbered and excluded.

entries.selected_sense: Successfully dealing with a problem or disagreement, represented by solving a login problem with support.
entries.difficulty_rationale: Oxford selected sense 1 carries B2 metadata and a B2 discussion/agreement topic. Collins corroborates the problem-solving meaning but shows no selected CEFR label. Propose B2 without inventing a Collins level.
entries.excluded_scope: Making a firm personal decision, formal votes, determination as a noun, technical decomposition, musical resolution and resolving again are excluded.
entries.context_boundary: Foundation02.05 and surface uses involving software merging, room conflicts and construction decisions remain exact and pending. Lexical approval would not endorse technical procedures or the authored re/solve analysis.
entries.proposed_note: Proposed formal problem-solving verb with the retained login-problem example and editorial B2 supported by Oxford. Collins supplies meaning/register evidence without a displayed selected level. Morphology, specialized contexts and every other gate remain separate.

sources.other_sense_boundary: Deciding firmly and voting on a resolution are separately C2; those levels and senses are excluded.

sources.summary: Problem resolution means arriving at a solution. The source supports the retained support-team example at the lexical level.
sources.regional_register: The selected sense is marked formal with no regional restriction.
sources.other_sense_boundary: Firm decisions, the determination noun and resolving into a clearer form are separate; no selected CEFR label is displayed.

entries.selected_sense: Helping a person carry out an activity, represented by helping a visitor with a sign-in form.
entries.difficulty_rationale: Oxford selected helping-a-person sense 1 has B1 metadata and topic evidence. Collins selected task-help sense 1 is B2. Propose editorial B1 for the bounded visitor-help example while preserving the formal register and B2 disagreement.
entries.excluded_scope: Sports assists as nouns, assisted-living services, clinical or personal-care procedures, financial aid and a thing facilitating a process are not accepted under this ordinary verb proposal.
entries.context_boundary: Foundation02.08 remains pending because its collect pickup binding is held and its return use has no inferred borrowed-key acceptance. Assisted living remains a separate scored noun compound.
entries.proposed_note: Proposed formal ordinary help-with-an-activity verb with the original visitor/form example and editorial B1. Oxford B1 and Collins B2 remain explicit. Assisted living, held neighboring expressions and all nonlanguage gates remain separate.

sources.other_sense_boundary: Helping a process occur more easily is a separate sense 2. The sports noun is a separate entry.

entries.selected_sense: Checking truth or accuracy against evidence, represented by comparing a reference number with an order record.
entries.difficulty_rationale: Oxford checking sense 1 and confirming sense 2 both carry C1. The selected checking sense also has a C1 scientific-research topic. Collins shows no selected level. No inspected evidence justifies draft A2 or a B2 clamp.
entries.hold_reason: Hold the full entry pending independent level and selected-sense confirmation. The current establish-accuracy wording should be considered against the source distinction between checking and asserting/confirming truth; no rewrite is silently accepted.
entries.excluded_scope: Legal verification, scientific validation, authentication/security guarantees and confirming a statement without the selected checking activity are not approved.
entries.context_boundary: Preserve every verify surface context, including the inherited verified-status-page hold, privacy, legal, account and security contexts. Foundation02.04 and the authored veri/fy analysis remain pending.
entries.proposed_note: Held unchanged. The selected Oxford C1 level and absent Collins label do not support draft A2. Checking versus confirming scope needs independent consideration. No note, source reference, gate or other field is proposed for integration.

entries.selected_sense: Finding where a person or thing is, represented by searching for an original document.
entries.difficulty_rationale: Oxford selected find-position sense 1 has B1 metadata. Collins selected sense 1 is B2 and formal. Propose editorial B1 for the retained document-finding example while recording the level/register disagreement; Collins separate siting sense B1+ is not used.
entries.excluded_scope: Putting or building something in a location, establishing a business, located as an adjective, localization and technical identification procedures remain outside this selected finding sense.
entries.context_boundary: Four expression surface uses concern locating things or records; none currently scores this selected ID. Keep all focus lists and domain gates exact, with no new bindings.
entries.proposed_note: Proposed find-position verb with the original document example and editorial B1 from Oxford. Collins selected B2 and formal register remain explicit. Business siting, adjective uses, other expressions and nonlanguage approval remain separate.

sources.summary: The first sense discovers a person or item's position. The ordinary document-search example fits without requiring any specialized finding method.
sources.regional_register: No regional restriction is shown on the selected finding sense. The especially North American label belongs to business establishment sense 3.
sources.other_sense_boundary: Siting/building something and starting a business in a place are separate; their labels are not transferred.

sources.summary: The selected sense discovers where someone or something can be found, corroborating the current definition and document example.
sources.regional_register: The selected finding sense is formal. Mainly US/business applies only to separate sense 3.
sources.other_sense_boundary: Placing/building is separate sense 2 with B1+; that lower label is not evidence for the finding sense.

entries.selected_sense: Including a separate file with an electronic message, represented by attaching a form to an email.
entries.difficulty_rationale: Oxford email sense 2, attach_sng_6, has B1 metadata. Collins computing sense 5 also shows B1. Propose B1 using those exact electronic-file senses; physical joining levels and the unrelated B2 footer are not evidence.
entries.excluded_scope: Physical fastening, joining someone, emotional attachment, attributing importance or blame, attaching contractual conditions and legal seizure remain separate.
entries.context_boundary: The five matching expression texts do not expressly identify email/message attachment and must not acquire this scored ID. The completed form in the example grants no acceptance to complete's separate form-filling sense.
entries.proposed_note: Proposed electronic-file attachment sense only, retaining the form/email example with editorial B1. Oxford sense 2 and Collins sense 5 support B1. Physical attachments, ambiguous expression uses, completed-form sense transfer and all other gates remain excluded.

sources.summary: Sense 2 specifically adds an electronic document to an email. It is separately numbered from physical joining and carries its own B1 metadata.
sources.regional_register: No regional restriction is displayed for the email sense.
sources.other_sense_boundary: The rendered Phones/email/internet B1 topic is attached to sense 1, not independently displayed on sense 2. The selected B1 comes from sense 2 HTML metadata.

sources.summary: The computing sense includes a file as a separate part of a message. This supports the retained file/email meaning and selected B1 placement.
sources.regional_register: The selected sense is labelled computing, with no regional restriction. This is everyday file-message vocabulary, not systems/security approval.
sources.other_sense_boundary: Physical joining in sense 1 also shows B1 but is not selected. Contract conditions and attributed qualities are separate.
